title: Lemma `lem:miraPi` sketched + terminology error (bottom submodule vs top quotient)

comments.author: human
comments.body:
`lem:miraPi` (§2.1) asserts, for generic irreducible admissible $\Pi$ on $\mathrm{GL}_{n+1}$:
(i) $W\mapsto W|_{P_{n+1}}$ is injective, and (ii) its image contains $\mathcal C_c^\infty(N_{n+1}\backslash P_{n+1},\psi^{-1})$.

Both are true standard facts, but the current proof is a one-paragraph sketch and contains a genuine **terminology error**: it calls $\operatorname{ind}_{N_{n+1}}^{P_{n+1}}\psi^{-1}$ the "top quotient / highest derivative piece." In the Bernstein–Zelevinsky filtration of $\Pi|_{P_{n+1}}$, the object $\operatorname{ind}_{N_{n+1}}^{P_{n+1}}\psi^{-1}=(\Phi^+)^n\Psi^+(\Pi^{(n+1)})$ is the **bottom submodule** ($k=n+1$), not the top quotient.

**What Grounding requires.** State precisely, with hypotheses verified:
- For generic $\Pi$, the highest derivative $\Pi^{(n+1)}\neq 0$ (this is the *definition/characterization* of genericity), so the bottom BZ submodule is $\cong\operatorname{ind}_{N_{n+1}}^{P_{n+1}}\psi^{-1}=\mathcal C_c^\infty(N_{n+1}\backslash P_{n+1},\psi^{-1})$.
- Under $\Pi\hookrightarrow\mathcal W(\Pi,\psi^{-1})$ this submodule is realized as $\{W: W|_{P_{n+1}}\in\mathcal C_c^\infty(N_{n+1}\backslash P_{n+1},\psi^{-1})\}$, giving claim (ii).
- Injectivity (i): a generic irreducible $\Pi$ is generated under $P_{n+1}$ from its mirabolic restriction, and Whittaker functions are determined by their values on $P_{n+1}$ (Kirillov model).

Cite with exact references: Bernstein–Zelevinsky, Ann. Sci. ENS 10 (1977), §3–5, Thm. 5.20; JPSS, Amer. J. Math. 105 (1983), §2; Cogdell–Piatetski-Shapiro (Kirillov model). Replace the sketch by a statement that names the theorem, verifies the genericity hypothesis, and derives (i),(ii).
